reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not practitioner/legal approval
experience_basis: Packages 16/20/21 reconciled against current lesson wording
findings: Current lesson is usable if hazard/exposure/risk concepts remain separated from Crew Blueprint's instructional behavior/control framing. Do not attribute the whole diagram as one OSHA taxonomy.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not practitioner approval
experience_basis: Package 20 gap audit and current lesson comparison
findings: NCCE can remain as Crew Blueprint instructional architecture. Near-miss/reporting facts should retain external evidence; NCCE itself must not be described as a national or OSHA standard.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not workplace PPE approval
experience_basis: Current Module 3 wording reconciled with OSHA PPE sources and Packages 16/20A
findings: Modules 3.1–3.2 remain directionally sound when every listed PPE item is treated as task/site/hazard dependent. Remove or qualify examples that imply venue height or job title alone triggers a specific PPE requirement.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not workplace PPE approval
experience_basis: Current lesson compared with OSHA PPE framework
findings: The current coaching sentence saying a production direction to change clothing means the hazard assessment changed is too strong. Production appearance requirements and hazard-selected PPE may change independently; later learner-facing revision should separate them explicitly.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — requires experienced truck-loader/production-logistics review
equipment_jurisdiction_context: Trailer/dock load-in awareness; no driver/load-acceptance authority
findings: Current language turns one possible trailer sequence into a universal physics rule and includes contradictory front/rear phrasing. Retain only the transferable rule: follow the responsible loader's sequence and do not bypass restraints/cargo-control decisions independently.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — requires material-handling practitioner review
findings: Visibility/control concept is strong. The current 'two-person standard' for tall cases is too universal; later copy should say use the assigned method/additional help/route control appropriate to the actual load and route.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — requires adult material-handling practitioner/ergonomics review
equipment_jurisdiction_context: Manual team handling; no powered/rigging/overhead work
findings: Team coordination and pinch-point awareness belong in Foundation, but current prescriptive ramp/body-position and 'side pressure' instructions are too universal for a general online course. Replace later with bounded recognition, stop/escalate and employer-assigned method language.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — requires tool/equipment practitioner review
findings: Keep obvious-defect reporting and do-not-work-around-damage principles. Remove the absolute 'there is always a replacement' statement and avoid generic function-testing instructions on unfamiliar equipment; exact inspection/testing belongs to the applicable item/process.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — requires practitioner review
experience_basis: SFS-U01 team-handling evidence and current Module 7.3 comparison
findings: One clearly understood current-call method and stopping on conflicting direction are sound. Exact caller location, command words and countdown sequence should remain examples/site-specific rather than universal procedure.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not department practitioner approval
experience_basis: Package 17, MDQ authority model and current Module 9 examples
findings: The support-vs-technical boundary is strong. Object categories must stay heuristic: actual permission is determined by assignment, ownership, system state and controlling authority, not visual appearance or category name alone.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — needs employer/practitioner validation
experience_basis: Package 19 callback findings compared with current Module 10.2
findings: Reliability/professionalism as recurring callback factors is supportable. The current example that specialization may occur after '5–10 calls' is not established as a transferable industry threshold and should be removed or explicitly labeled illustrative.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — needs employer/local/practitioner validation
findings: Current boundary against self-authorizing specialist work is strong. The statement that specialization begins only when a worker is 'invited' is too narrow; hiring, training, apprenticeship/referral, supervised assignment and credential pathways can also create legitimate progression.
